row.evidence: Splashtop's help centre says "Splashtop / Okta provisioning is supported with Splashtop Enterprise" and Team Settings lists "SCIM Provisioning Token (Only available in Enterprise)"; Enterprise is "Contact us for customizable licensing and pricing".
row.notes: Unchanged from June: SCIM and SAML SSO are Enterprise-only (Contact Sales). Remote Access pricing: Solo $6/mo (single user), Pro $8.25/u/mo ($99/yr), Performance $13/u/mo ($149/yr), all billed annually. The pricing page does not name SCIM; the plan gate comes from Splashtop's help centre. SSO must be set up first (each provisioned user carries an ssoName SCIM extension attribute naming the Splashtop SSO method). SCIM base URL is /scim/v1 although the extension URN and OneLogin template are SCIM 2.0. OneLogin uses OneLogin's generic SCIM v2 app, not a Splashtop catalogue app. Google Workspace: custom SAML app plus JIT only. Open API (users, groups, roles, licences, logs) is Enterprise-only.

plans.name: Solo
plans.notes: Single user; not a team plan.

plans.name: Enterprise
plans.price_text: Contact us for customizable licensing and pricing

scim.notes: Version 2.0 inferred from the urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:Splashtop:2.0 extension and the OneLogin 'SCIM v2 Enterprise' template; the URL path itself is /scim/v1.

auth.token_source: my.splashtop.com > Management > Settings > SCIM Provisioning Token > Set up an API token > Generate

operations.notes: deactivate left null: Okta's OIN page lists Deactivate, but Splashtop's own Okta article says removal deletes or removes the user from the team. JumpCloud's page says PATCH is unsupported and PUT cannot change 'active'.

deprovision.data_retained: Deleting a user removes them from the Splashtop team but does not delete their Splashtop account; they can still log in and buy their own subscription.

custom.how: Required extension attribute urn:ietf:params:scim:schemas:extension:Splashtop:2.0:User:ssoName set to the Splashtop SSO method name

attributes.notes: Microsoft's Entra tutorial maps userName, active, displayName, name.givenName, name.familyName, externalId and the ssoName extension for users, and displayName, externalId, members for groups (see idp_apps.entra).

limitations.text: Username/email cannot be updated via SCIM.
Users in multiple synced groups switch between groups unless multi-group membership is enabled in team settings.
SSO method must exist first; every provisioned user needs the ssoName attribute.
Per JumpCloud: PATCH unsupported, PUT cannot change active, DELETE hard-deletes users and groups, users cannot be filtered by email.

auth.notes: API tokens are created by team owners/super admins with a scope and expiry date and can be restricted to read-only; OAuth 2.0 apps are provisioned by Splashtop on request (access token 24 h, refresh token 30 days).

endpoints.purpose: Invite a user to the team
Delete a user from the team

rate_limits.text: User list queries are limited to 5000 user IDs at a time; no request rate limit documented.

limitations.text: Open API is only supported on Splashtop Enterprise subscriptions.

okta.notes: OIN page markup checks SAML, SWA, OIDC, SCIM, Create, Update, Deactivate, Group Push and Group Linking.

google.notes: Splashtop documents Google Workspace only as a custom SAML app with JIT; no Google provisioning is documented.

onelogin.notes: Splashtop's guide uses OneLogin's generic 'SCIM Provisioner with SAML (SCIM v2 Enterprise, full SAML)' app; OneLogin's own catalogue was not checked.

open_questions: Docs do not say whether SCIM deprovisioning frees the licence seat or ends active sessions.
SCIM filtering, pagination, discovery endpoints (ServiceProviderConfig/Schemas) and rate limits are not documented by Splashtop.
Whether a Splashtop role can be set via SCIM is not documented.
SCIM token expiry is not documented (Entra calls it a long-lived bearer token).
